change: A likely fix for Dwarf Heroes that would not throw uphill. In The Fallen Lords the hero's bottle throw has a throwing speed of 92 with a random spread of minus 81, and the converter copied that. Myth II has no negative spread in any of Bungie's or Magma's attacks, and Magma's own port of this throw has none, so it is now 0: the hero always throws at 92 (an ordinary dwarf throws at 66 to 74). The Dwarven Pathfinder's bottle throw had the same setting and gets the same fix. The teal Yearling pieces are not fixed yet: the chunks are trow pieces (the Forest Giants' pieces break into them when hit) drawn without the trow's colouring, and we need one more test in the game before choosing a fix.
test: Dwarf Heroes: can they throw uphill now, without walking up to the spot first? Downhill and on flat ground still fine?
Dwarven Pathfinders (if a level has them): the same question for their bottle throw.
Forest Giants and Old Growth Forest Giants: when one dies and its pieces are blown up, are the chunks teal like the Yearlings'? (We expect yes.)
If you can still run The Fallen Lords itself: what colour are those chunks there?

change: Heals should work now. Myth II refuses to let an ability be used on friendly units unless it says so, and The Fallen Lords never had that setting, so converted Journeymen and Heron Guards could heal neither other units nor themselves. A special ability that fires a healing projectile now carries the setting, as it does in Bungie's own Journeymen and Heron Guards. This also covers the Yearlings' mandrake heal, which is less certain.
test: Journeymen and Heron Guards: can they heal themselves? Other units, friend and foe?
Yearlings: can they heal themselves with the mandrake root? Can they heal others? They should not be able to, by the map makers' design.
Forest Giants and Trow (0.17): do they attack men now?
Anything else that can heal or help friendly units and does not work.

change: Two bugs found that may be why Forest Giants and Trow never attacked. First, every unit was marked giant-sized in Myth II (the converter read The Fallen Lords' AI-intelligence setting as the size); now only the Forest Giant and the trow are, as in Bungie's and Magma's versions, and everyone else is man-sized. Second, each attack's flags were copied raw, which scrambled the bits that say whether an attack is for giants or not for giants; they are now translated, so the Forest Giant's and trow's attacks come out exactly as in Bungie's own tags.
test: Forest Giants, Old Growth Forest Giants, Yearlings and Trow: do they attack men now? Giants?
Do other units now attack giants, and do giants take damage as before?
Does anything else behave differently since units stopped being giant-sized: movement, being knocked back, being crowded?
Unit height line-ups against the Butcher's shop: any unit that now looks the wrong size?
The change list has the size and attack-flag rows, if you want to check them.

change: A likely fix for units jogging on the spot after they stop. The Fallen Lords leaves each unit's pause and turning animations empty, and Myth II plays the pause animation when a unit stops. Bungie's own Myth II versions of the same units fill them, with the unit's idle and moving animations; the converter now does the same. Also new, because Keep asked for it: after converting, you can save a change list, every setting the converter wrote in each unit with its old value, its new value and why, to check the converter's work.
test: Moonwalking: do units stand still when they stop now, without pressing the space bar?
Turning: do units look right when they turn on the spot?
Change list: save it after converting and open it in a spreadsheet. Is anything in it wrong, unclear or missing?
Forest Giants and Trow (0.15): do they attack now?
Explosions (0.14): is the ground still black after satchels and wights?

change: Each unit now gets the pathfinding room Project Magma's port gives it, instead of one value for every unit. The Forest Giant gets 220 and the trow 154, where both had 77, which may be why they would not attack. Of the 17 monster settings Myth II has and The Fallen Lords does not, these are the only two that differ between units in Magma's port.
test: Forest Giants and Trow: do they attack now when ordered to? If not, what do they do: walk up and stand, turn away, or not move at all?
Movement: do big units get stuck or bunch up more or less than before?
Explosions (0.14): is the ground still black or streaky after satchels and wights?
Unit size (0.13): do thrall in deep water sit low now?

change: A likely fix for the black or streaky ground after explosions. Keep sent the same converted map before and after saving it in Loathing, and the main thing Loathing rewrites is the map's level-of-detail data. The converter wrote it as zeros. No map made by Bungie or Project Magma has a single zero there, so the converter now writes what Loathing writes.
test: Explosions: convert a plugin again with this version, then set off satchels, wights and fireballs. Is the ground still black, streaky or mirrored afterwards?
If it is, which level, and does saving the map in Loathing still cure it?
Unit size (0.13): do thrall in deep water sit low now? Does any unit look too small or too large?
Multiplayer: do the flags and balls appear in their own games? Does Assassin work on Sir Mauriac's two Bagrada in Winter maps?

change: Units are now drawn at Myth II's size. They were about a third too large, so thrall stood out of the water. Myth II's own files hold the thrall, dwarf, ghol, soulless and spider of The Fallen Lords with the same pictures, and Bungie drew each at 0.73 of its old size; converted units now get the same. Ambient sounds are also converted, and one damaged part of a plugin no longer stops the whole conversion.
test: Unit size: do units look the right size next to trees, buildings and each other? Do thrall standing in deep water now sit low in it, as in The Fallen Lords?
Wild River in Sir Mauriac's Tale is a good level to check thrall in water.
Any unit that now looks too small or too large: name it and the level. Villagers and Shades are the likeliest.
Multiplayer: do the flags and balls appear in their own games (0.12)? Does Assassin work on Sir Mauriac's two Bagrada in Winter maps?
Explosions: the black or streaky ground after satchels and wights is still being worked on.

change: Free-for-all and team maps now use Myth II's own flags and balls. The copies the converter made were not recognised by the game, so a hosted game still showed no flags or balls even after 0.11 made the units and scenery appear.
test: Multiplayer: host free-for-all, team, capture-the-flag and king-of-the-hill games on a converted map, with co-operative play off. Do the flags and balls appear in their own games now, and work as flags and balls?
Game types: name any game type where something is wrong, such as a flag in the wrong game, a missing assassin target, or a unit that should not be there.
Explosions: the black or streaky ground after satchels and wights is still being worked on.
Levels: does every level start? Name any that won't load.

change: Free-for-all and team maps now tell Myth II which game types their units, scenery, flags and balls belong to. Before, every one was marked as appearing in no game, so a hosted game started with no teams, flags or balls and ended at once. Keep found the cause.
Converted maps now say they are Myth II maps. They used to keep The Fallen Lords' version number, which made Myth II's editor Oak refuse them and may have made the game treat them as older maps.

The deck of Crow's Bridge's bridge is drawn again, so units crossing it no longer seem to walk on air, and the arch is dark underneath as in The Fallen Levels v2. The ground's markings are now translated to Myth II's meanings instead of copied from The Fallen Lords, on every map.
The ground beside bridges and other buildings no longer hides their walls. On Crow's Bridge it now meets the bridge's stone sides instead of sagging away below the railings.
Fixed a crash when scrolling to the edge of some maps, such as Crow's Bridge and crazyglue's Along the way to... The border at each map edge is also as wide as in The Fallen Lords again.
Buildings and other 3D models now appear, such as houses, barns, inns and bridges, and units walk around them.
Plants, bushes and units sit on the ground instead of floating above it or sinking into it.
Fixed missing unit sounds that stopped some levels from loading, such as On the road to Strand in Sir Mauriac's Tale.
Hills and slopes are smooth, not stepped.
Water now acts as water: units wade and slow down instead of walking on it.
First beta: convert a plugin in your browser.
